programs.title: Wild London
programs.desc: A famous naturalist reveals the nature present in the landscape of his native London.It presents extraordinary stories taking place in the center of the metropolis, including:peregrine falcons nesting on the parliament building.

programs.title: Making Life on Earth: Attenborough's Greatest Adventure
programs.desc: Sir David Attenborough, a great advocate of wildlife and popularizer of science, celebrates his 100th birthday.On this occasion, BBC Earth presents the extraordinary journey of this outstanding naturalist and traveler.

programs.title: Blue Planet 2
programs.desc: More than seven years have passed since the premiere of the second season of the nature super-production, but it still impresses with its great implementation.Its creators completed 125 expeditions in 39 countries over four years.They spent over six thousand hours diving in the depths and filming the coasts.The best scenes were selected from this spectacular material, taking viewers to inaccessible worlds.Their guide is Sir David Attenborough, who claims that we know less about the depths of our own planet than about the surface of Mars.The inhabitants of the ocean's depths influence our lives because they shape the climate and produce about half of the oxygen necessary for the functioning of the planet.They are also home to numerous representatives of the fauna kingdom.The development of technology has allowed man to look into their world, which was previously inaccessible.Scientists are also constantly expanding their knowledge of animal behavior.The first episode of the program is a journey through the waters surrounding the Seychelles, New Zealand, Japan and the Arctic.Filmmakers captured, among others, dolphins surfing in the Red Sea.They tracked walruses resting on melting ice in the Arctic.They followed killer whales and humpback whales feasting on herring schools in Norway.

programs.title: Blue Planet 2
programs.desc: For centuries, humanity has believed that the oceans are so vast and their inhabitants are so numerous that human activity cannot harm them.It is now known that this is not true.The existence of many animal species associated with the ocean ecosystem is at risk.This is clearly visible in the example of herring.Overfishing wiped out their population 50 years ago.Currently, thanks to good management, it has been reborn.Human-made noise, industrial pollution and plastic waste also negatively impact ocean life.In turn, more than 2/3 of the world's coral reefs have suffered from global warming.Recent research has revealed that the chemical composition of ocean waters is changing.They become acidic due to carbon dioxide dissolving in them.
